input.summary:
Bedroom 3 furnished in parts/room-17.mjs: white bed on the west wall, wardrobe of four barrels, dark-oak writing table and chair under the front window, red rug, lantern on a nightstand, a standing floor lantern, a candle and a hanging lantern on a chain. The test copy lights every floor cell (min 8, 0 dark) and fits, but the walk can't yet reach the room (the stair and hall aren't built in the shared build).
The real make.sh build REFUSES all 28 of my writes: the mansion shell's fill(..., "air") (shell.mjs:27) puts air over every room interior and runParts' lock treats that air as placed. So build.nbt is whole but contains none of this room.
I did not bypass the lock. The fix belongs in the shell: leave interior cells unset rather than filling them with air.
left: Blocked in the real build: mansion shell (parts/shell.mjs:27) fills every room interior with air, so runParts refuses all 28 furnishing writes for bedroom 3 (and every other room). The shell must leave interior cells unset (the grid's default is air) or carve only the openings; then re-run make.sh and confirm this part's line shows no REFUSED.

Walk verdict in the shared build is UNREACHABLE (0 of 49 cells): the grand stair and upper hall must be built by the stair joiner and shell so the east doorway x44 z46..47 and the south door z50 connect to the entrance. Verified only on a test copy outside the parts dir (/tmp/p24-test/run.mjs), not on build.nbt.

Chair stair facing: I used facing north (back to the south) on the assumption that stairs' facing is the open side; the render did not confirm it, so check it when the part is built into the real build.

Test harness /tmp/p24-test/run.mjs applies build() onto a copy of build.nbt without runParts; it is a workaround to verify the layout, not the pipeline. A plan.md Notes line records the shell air-fill blocker.

waste.what: Finding which earlier part owned my cells: I ran build.mjs with MCD_PARTS_CELLS (which expects a file path, not a flag) and grepped the cell dump by hand, then grepped shell.mjs for 'air'.
waste.tool: runParts should print, for each REFUSED write, the earlier part that owns the cell (e.g. 'owned by mansion shell') so a worker doesn't have to dump cell maps.

waste.what: Verifying the furnishing on a copy because the lock blocked the real build: I wrote a harness that calls build(g) on load(build.nbt) directly to get the room check and render.
waste.cost: one harness file and two runs
waste.tool: a mcd or runParts option such as --unlock-air or a 'dry' run that reports refusals without the lock, so the room check can run against the real layout.

waste.what: Writing the furniture as one layers() call per y-level with hand-indexed 7-character rows, and placing the bed separately with bed().
waste.cost: about 40 cells worked out by hand; one legend key (L) was missing and needed a fix
waste.tool: layers() could take a 3D layout string with a per-character legend and warn when a legend key is unused or missing from the legend, instead of silently skipping it.

waste.what: Reading the plan's floor grid and the room's coordinates, then working out the lane, door-cell and window-cell clearance by hand.
waste.tool: mcd plan could mark the clearance cells (doorway first cells, window first cells) as '~' so the lanes don't need working out by hand.

companions.task: Change parts/shell.mjs:27 so the main block's interiors are left unset (grid air) instead of filled with air, so the room furnishers can write into their rooms; the mason owns the lock question with the runParts maintainers.
Confirm the grand stair and upper hall connect the entrance to the upper floor, so the bedroom 3 walk verdict can say reachable.
Review the room's light (min 8, no dark cell) and say whether the desk lantern and the hanging lantern read as one scheme in the real build.
